description_full: Nokia Oyj, together with its subsidiaries, provides mobile, fixed, and cloud network solutions in North and Latin America, Greater China, India, Asia Pacific, Europe, the Middle East, and Africa. It operates in four segments: Network Infrastructure, Mobile Networks, Cloud and Network Services, and Nokia Technologies. The company offers fixed network solutions, such as fiber and copper technologies, access infrastructure, in-home Wi-Fi solutions, and cloud and virtualization services; IP network solutions, which delivers IP edge routing and data center networking solutions for residential, mobile, enterprise, and cloud applications; and optical networks solutions, which provides optical transport networks for metro, regional, and long-haul applications. It also provides mobile technology products, agentic AI platform, and services for radio access networks and microwave radio links for transport networks; and network management solutions, as well as network planning, optimization, network deployment, and technical support services. In addition, the company offers cloud and network services, including open, secure, automated, and scalable software and solutions; and 5G core, secure autonomous networks, private wireless and industrial edge, and network APIs. Further, it licenses intellectual property, including patents, technologies, and the Nokia brand. The company serves its products and services to defense communications energy and resources, enterprise and industrial campus, private networks, public sector, and transportation industries. Nokia Oyj was founded in 1865 and is headquartered in Espoo, Finland.

financial_summary: Nokia Corporation Sponsored is a large-cap technology business with a $43.3B market cap on $22.2B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at -5% over the past three years, and a shrinking top line is the hardest headwind any business can overcome.
Returns on capital run at 10% against a 9% cost of capital, which means the business barely earns its keep economically, with gross margins sitting at 39%.

The business throws off $1.6B in free cash flow — roughly 7 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 3.14× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and interest coverage runs at 3.6×.
Shareholder yield is only 1.3%, a thin return of capital, and insiders hold 3.1% of the shares, and profit capture is only 0.2× the fair share, suggesting no structural edge inside its industry.

sect: Its 4% operating margin is roughly in line with the Technology median (7%).

Over five years it has been losing share of the sector profit pool (-14.5% a year).
The sector is fragmented and competitive (HHI 0.03 across 530 companies in the universe; the top four hold 29% of revenue), so pricing power is hard to come by.
mkt: The shares are in a strong uptrend, up 59% over the past year excluding the latest month, though it has pulled back 21% over the last three months.
The price sits near the bottom of its 52-week range, 56% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 62% and a beta of 0.92, it moves roughly with the market, though its beta has shifted (1y 1.75 vs 5y 0.88), so read it loosely.
Liquidity is deep, with about $706.9M traded a day.
In past sell-offs it fell 45% in the 2020 crash, 33% in the 2022 bear market and 76% in 2008.
val: The stock trades 35% below its DCF fair value of $11.80, a meaningful margin of safety.
The fair-value models corroborate one another (dispersion 9%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $8.28 to $17.26 (P10-P90).
On multiples it looks expensive against Technology peers: P/E 47.9 vs 26.7 (sector median).
Against its own history it is dear: the EBIT multiple sits 167% above its 10-year median.
Earnings yields are thin: an FCF yield of 3.8% (below the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 2.4% (vs the 8% bar).
The 12 covering analysts target $14.52 on average, 90% above the price.
prof: ROIC of 10% earns above the cost of capital of 9.2%, but the 1pp spread is short of the 7pp moat bar; returns have swung a lot from year to year (CV 0.98).
It runs a 39% gross margin and converts 7% of revenue into free cash flow.
Earnings quality looks solid: cash conversion of 3.14x.
ROE of 3% comes mostly from margins and asset turnover rather than leverage (1.8x equity multiplier).
hlth: The balance sheet carries net cash of $3.9B.
growth: Revenue has compounded at -5.0% over 3 years and -2.1% over 5 years, so the decline is deepening.
At current returns, reinvesting 100% of profits supports about 9.8% a year of fundamental growth, enough to sustain growth.
Free cash flow has compounded 2.5% a year over five years, short of the 5% durability bar.
It has beaten earnings estimates by 19.1% on average.
Analysts expect 16.6% long-term annual earnings growth.
own: Insiders own a modest 3.1%, and institutions hold 16%.
Shareholder yield is a modest 1.3% (1.7% in dividends, less 0.6% of net share issuance).
It pays out 100% of earnings, more than it earns, so the dividend is at risk.
people: With about 78,005 employees, each generates about $284K of revenue, 0.8x the Technology median.
That works out to $21K of free cash flow per employee.
CEO pay is $7.1M (25x revenue per employee).
